Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four. The c. 215 treatises that survive today mainly deal with alchemy and chemistry, magic, and Shi'ite religious philosophy.
Which one below was established earliest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
MUMPS (published 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Robert Aumann is a mathematician. Aumann received the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 2005 for his work on conflict and cooperation through game theory analysis.
What is the atomic number of Rhodium?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
What is the atomic number of Argon?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
In what year was Alan Turing born?
Alan Turing: Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
In what year was Scurvy discovered?
Scurvy or scorbutus is a deficiency disease (state of malnutrition) resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
In what year was Polonium discovered?
Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84.
Spironolactone: Pfizer. Spironolactone, sold under the brand name Aldactone among others, is classed as a diuretic medication.
In which country did the Chengdu J-10 take place?

Chengdu J-10: People's Republic of China. It is produced by the Chengdu Aircraft Corporation (CAC) for the People's Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) of China, and exported to the Pakistan Air Force (PAF).
Who is credited with discovering Seaborgium?
Seaborgium: Yuri Oganessian. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrogen cyanide?
Hydrogen cyanide: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula H−C≡N.
Who is credited with discovering Tungsten?
Tungsten: Juan José Elhuyar. Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
This genus of succulent, spiky-leaved plants native to the arid Americas typically takes years to mature, with each rosette flowering only once before dying — what's the genus called?
Agave (Anglo-Hispanic) is a genus of monocots native to the arid regions of the Americas.
In 1978, a run-in with a particle accelerator's proton beam left this Russian physicist with an extraordinary survival story after it passed straight through his head — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski (born 25 June 1942) is a Russian retired particle physicist.
This red giant is the brightest star in the constellation Boötes and the fourth-brightest star in the entire night sky — name the star?
Arcturus is a red giant star in the northern constellation of Botes, and the brightest star in the constellation.
The only mammals capable of true sustained flight, members of this order — the second largest among mammals — fly using long digits webbed by a thin membrane. What are they?
Bat (order Chiroptera) are winged mammals, the only mammals capable of true and sustained flight.
Native to cool parts of Europe and Asia, this deciduous shrub produces small, glossy black berries especially rich in vitamin C and vulnerable to cold snaps during spring flowering — name the fruit?
Blackcurrant (Ribes nigrum), black currant or cassis is a deciduous shrub in the family Grossulariaceae grown for its edible berries.
Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide and often striking during sleep, this parafunctional habit grinds teeth and clenches jaws until enamel wears away — what's it called?
Bruxism is excessive teeth grinding or jaw clenching.

Which German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist discovered oxygen — though Priestley published first — and identified elements like molybdenum, tungsten, and chlorine before reportedly dying of mercury poisoning?
Carl Wilhelm Scheele (9 December 1742 - 21 May 1786) was a German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist.

Sold under the brand name Thorazine, this phenothiazine antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder — but it's also been used for nausea, pre-surgery anxiety, and even stubborn hiccups. What is it?
Chlorpromazine (CPZ), marketed under the brand names Thorazine and Largactil among others, is an antipsychotic medication.
Native to Asia but so invasive in Australian cities that it was dubbed 'Most Important Pest/Problem' in 2008, which urban-adapted bird species is this?
Common myna (Acridotheres tristis), sometimes spelled mynah, is a bird in the family Sturnidae, native to Asia.
This bluish-purple discoloration of the skin, most visible on the lips, nail beds, and ear lobes, signals a drop in oxygen bound to hemoglobin in the blood — name the condition?
Cyanosis is the change of tissue color to a bluish-purple hue, as a result of decrease in the amount of oxygen bound to the hemoglobin in the red blood cells of the capillary bed.
Bred around 1890 in Thuringia by a tax collector seeking a loyal protector, this German working-dog breed is known in North America by a slightly different two-word name — which breed?
Dobermann is a German breed of medium-large working dog of pinscher type.

This German chess champion — also a mathematician and philosopher — held the world title for 27 years, the longest reign ever, and was famed for a 'psychological' approach said to unsettle opponents. Who was he?
Emanuel Lasker (German; December 24, 1868 - January 11, 1941) was a German chess player, mathematician, and philosopher.

This front-of-the-head feature found in humans and other animals houses most of the sense organs, including the eyes, nose, and mouth, and its damage can profoundly affect one's sense of identity — name this body part?
Face is the front of the head in humans and many other animals that features most of the sense organs including the eyes, nose and mouth.
Having led Renault, Sauber, and Alfa Romeo's F1 outfits, this French engineer took the reins at Ferrari as team principal in 2023 — who is he?
Fred Vasseur (French; born 28 May 1968) is a French motorsport executive, businessman and engineer.

Colorless, odorless, and oddly sweet, this viscous sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of every triglyceride in animal fat, and moonlights as a food sweetener — what is it?
Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.
Hailed by Time as a 2019 'Pioneer' yet condemned as a mad scientist, which Chinese biophysicist announced in 2018 that he'd created the first gene-edited human babies?
He Jiankui (pinyin: H Jinku HUH KWAY; born 1984) is a Chinese biophysicist known for his controversial first use of genome editing in humans in 2018.
While first described from Virginia, this genus of flowering shrubs reaches its greatest diversity in East Asia, and some species climb up to 30 metres by scaling trees. What plant is it?
Hydrangea (or) is a genus of more than 70 species of flowering plants native to Asia and the Americas.
These creatures don't breathe through a nose or lungs — air enters through tiny paired openings along their sides, piped straight to the tissues. What hexapod group are they?
Insect (from Latin insectum) are hexapod invertebrates of the class Insecta.
This financier's 1999 bestseller on mutual funds became an investment classic after he founded a low-cost investing giant — who is he?

John C. Bogle (May 8, 1929 - January 16, 2019) was an American investor, business magnate and philanthropist who was the founder of The Vanguard Group and is credited with popularizing the index fund.
Alongside Robert Goddard and Hermann Oberth, this reclusive Russian scientist who lived in a log house near Kaluga is considered a founding father of modern rocketry — who is he?

This scientific discipline studies language through areas like syntax, semantics, morphology, and phonology, with subfields examining its biological roots and psychological underpinnings — name the field?
Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguistics encompasses many branches and subfields that span both theoretical and practical applications.

With degrees from Stanford in chemical engineering and a medical degree from Cornell, this physician-astronaut spent nearly eight days aboard Endeavour in 1992, becoming the first African-American woman in space — who is she?
Mae Jemison (born October 17, 1956) is an American engineer, physician, and former NASA astronaut.
Most common on the legs in women and the back in men, this cancer develops from melanin-producing skin cells and, in extremely rare cases, can even arise in the lungs — which cancer?
Melanoma is a type of cancer, typically skin cancer; it develops from the melanin-producing cells known as melanocytes.
These cylindrical, burrowing insects have small eyes and shovel-like front limbs highly adapted for digging underground — name the family?
Mole cricket are members of the insect family Gryllotalpidae, in the order Orthoptera (grasshoppers, locusts, and crickets).
This flexible body part lets the head turn in every direction while its compartments guard the spinal cord and upper airway between head and torso — what is it, also known as the cervix?
Neck is the part of the body in many vertebrates that connects the head to the torso.
Named after a German physicist, this SI unit of electrical resistance is represented by the uppercase Greek letter omega — name the unit?
Ohm (symbol:, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).

This skin sensation — often described as tingling, prickling, or numbness — is most familiar as the 'pins and needles' feeling after a limb falls asleep from staying still too long — name this sensation?
Paresthesia (or paraesthesia) is a sensation of the skin that may feel like numbness (hypoesthesia), tingling, pricking, chilling, or burning.
Colorless in acid and a vivid pink in base, which phthalein dye is the chemist's go-to indicator for acid-base titrations?
Phenolphthalein (feh-NOL(F)-th-leen) is a chemical compound with the formula C20H14O4 and is often written as "HIn", "HPh", "phph" or simply "Ph" in shorthand notation.

This academic field studies systems of governance and power, favoring descriptive and empirical analysis of behavior and institutions over the value judgments used in philosophy about the state — name the discipline?
Political science (sometimes abbreviated as poli sci) is a field which aims to study the scientific aspect of politics.

This medical specialty diagnoses, treats, and prevents disorders of cognition, perception, mood, emotion, and behavior, typically beginning assessment with a case history and mental status exam — name the field?
Psychiatry is the medical specialty devoted to the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of deleterious mental conditions.
One of the three ancient arts of discourse alongside grammar and logic, this discipline studies the techniques speakers and writers use to inform, persuade, and motivate an audience — what is it?
Rhetoric is the art of persuasion.
Which plant genus in the mint family, comprising nearly 1,000 species of shrubs and perennials, includes both a common cooking herb and — surprisingly — rosemary as one of its species?
Salvia is the largest genus of plants in the sage family Lamiaceae, with just under 1,000 species of shrubs, herbaceous perennials, and annuals.

Though many are crustaceans more closely related to insects than to fish, which group of exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates, including molluscs and echinoderms, is a leading cause of food allergies?
Shellfish are exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates used as food, including various species of molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms.

Extending from the base of the brainstem down to the lower back, this tubular bundle of nervous tissue is covered by the meninges and, together with the brain, makes up the central nervous system — name this structure?

Spinal cord is a long, thin, tubular structure made up of nervous tissue that extends from the medulla oblongata in the lower brainstem to the lumbar region of the vertebral column (backbone) of vertebrate animals.
Also called 'true comfrey,' this Boraginaceae perennial is native to damp European meadows and popular with bumblebees, despite carrying warnings about liver toxicity if eaten — which plant?
Symphytum officinale is a perennial flowering plant in the family Boraginaceae.
This condition causes abnormally low platelet levels in the blood, leading to prolonged or excessive bleeding — what blood disorder is it?
Thrombocytopenia is a condition characterized by abnormally low levels of platelets (also known as thrombocytes) in the blood.
The most widespread New World scavenger of its kind, this bird sniffs out the gases of early decay to find carrion and rides thermals instead of flapping — which bird?
Turkey vulture (Cathartes aura) is the most widespread of the New World vultures.

Its small molecule packs a surprising punch: strong polarity, relentless hydrogen bonding, and a starring role as the fluid of all known life and the main stuff of Earth's oceans — what compound is it?
Water is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula H2O.

Released from prison in June 2025 to resume leading Turkey's nationalist Victory Party, this politician previously served as deputy leader of the far-right Nationalist Movement Party in the mid-2010s — who is he?
Ümit Özdağ (born 3 March 1961) is a Turkish politician who returned to his position as the current leader of the Victory Party after being released from prison on 17 June 2025.
Nicknamed for the stripes on its legs and body, this day-biting mosquito native to Southeast Asia spreads dengue, yellow fever, and Chikungunya — what is it called?
Aedes albopictus: Species of mosquito. The insect is called a tiger mosquito as it has stripes, as does a tiger.

An anatomist and archaeologist turned TV presenter, she has served as professor of Public Engagement in Science at the University of Birmingham since 2012 and once led the charity Humanists UK — who is she?
Alice Roberts: English academic, TV presenter and author.
First named by Karl Friedrich Burdach in 1822, this paired brain structure tucked in the temporal lobes drives fear, anxiety, and aggression as part of the limbic system. What is it?
Amygdala: Paired structure within the brain temporal lobe.
Usually symptomless until it ruptures — causing sudden, severe abdominal or lower-back pain — this dangerous enlargement of the body's main artery is most common in the abdomen — what condition?
Aortic aneurysm: Excessive enlargement of the human aorta.
Born from acetylsalicylic acid, this everyday drug cools fevers within about 30 minutes and is taken long-term to fend off heart attacks and strokes by quieting platelets — what is it?

The most widespread bird in its family, found on every continent except Antarctica (where only stray vagrants appear), this species has blue upperparts, a deeply forked tail, and usually nests in man-made structures — what is it?
Barn swallow: Species of bird. The barn swallow (Hirundo rustica) is the most widespread species of swallow in the world, occurring on all continents, with vagrants reported even in Antarctica.
This interdisciplinary field examines moral questions raised by advances in biology, medicine, and biotechnology, touching everything from patient care to environmental policy — what is it called?
Bioethics: Study of the ethical issues emerging from advances in biology and medicine.
A synthetic group-7 transition metal made only in particle accelerators, this radioactive element honors a Danish physicist and sits at atomic number 107 — what is it?
Bohrium: Chemical element with atomic number 107 (Bh)

Known also as the Zambezi or Lake Nicaragua species, this aggressive fish can thrive in both salt and fresh water, having been tracked more than 1,100 kilometers up the Mississippi River — what animal is it?
Bull shark: Species of fish. Bull sharks are listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.
First classified by Linnaeus in 1753 and indigenous to Eastern Asia, this annual flowering plant has been cultivated throughout history for fiber, oil, food, and medicine — which plant?
Cannabis sativa: Plant species. It has been cultivated throughout recorded history and used as a source of industrial fiber, seed oil, food, and medicine.

Named from a Latin word meaning 'blind,' this pouch at the start of the large intestine sits on the same side of the body as the appendix and receives chyme straight from the small intestine — which structure?
Cecum: Pouch in the large intestine. It is typically located on the right side of the body (the same side of the body as the appendix, to which it is joined).
Native to the high Andes and living in colonies called 'herds,' this South American rodent boasts the densest fur of any land mammal — about 20,000 hairs per square centimeter. What is it?
Chinchilla: Rodent genus. The chinchilla is named after the Chincha people of the Andes, who once wore its dense, velvet-like fur and ate its meat.
With a coat of dusky-grey blotches that inspired its common name, this wild cat is one of the few able to climb down tree trunks head-first, using a long tail for balance — what species is it?

Clouded leopard: Species of wild cat. Its head-and-body length ranges from 68.6 to 108 cm (27.0 to 42.5 in) with a 61 to 91 cm (24 to 36 in) long tail, which it uses for balancing when moving in trees.
Often defined as the transmission of information, this concept is famously modeled as a source encoding a message, sending it through a channel, and a receiver decoding it — what is it?
Communication: Transmission of information. Models of communication are simplified overviews of its main components and their interactions.
A group of these black birds is famously called a 'murder,' and their larger cousins are known as ravens — what bird is this?
Crow: Index of animals with the same common name.
Named for a 19th-century British mathematician, this pair of logic rules shows how 'and' and 'or' swap places under negation — what are they called?
De Morgan's laws: Pair of logical equivalences.

Sudden lower-abdominal pain, sometimes a 'smoldering' slow burn over days — and the trouble is little abnormal pouches inflaming in the wall of your large intestine. What gastrointestinal disease is this?
Diverticulitis: Digestive disease of the large intestine. People may experience a single attack, repeated attacks, or ongoing "smoldering" diverticulitis.
Having studied mathematics under Karl Weierstrass, which philosopher founded the school of phenomenology and argued that transcendental consciousness sets the limits of all possible knowledge?
Coiled to just 6 to 7 centimetres but stretching nearly 20 feet if unraveled, this tube connects each testicle to the vas deferens and stores maturing sperm — what is it?

Epididymis: Tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens. The epididymis serves as an interconnection between the multiple efferent ducts at the rear of a testicle (proximally), and the vas deferens (distally).
The most widely distributed member of its subfamily, this semiaquatic, fish-eating mustelid ranges across Europe, much of Asia, and North Africa's Maghreb — which animal?
Made by nearly every living organism, this protein locks iron away in a safe, soluble form inside cells, and its blood level is the standard test doctors use for anemia or iron overload — what is it?
Ferritin: Iron-carrying protein. Ferritin is a universal intracellular and extracellular protein that stores iron and releases it in a controlled fashion.
As commander of Apollo 8, he led the first crew to circle the Moon and earned the Congressional Space Medal of Honor — who is he?
Frank Borman: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1928–2023)
Pioneered by Gregor Mendel's 19th-century pea plant experiments in Brno, this branch of biology studies heredity and trait inheritance — what is it?
Genetics: Science of genes, heredity and variation.
This type of organ produces an organism's sex hormones and gametes — testicles in males, ovaries in females — what is it called?
Gonad: Gland that produces sex cells.
This standard markup language structures web documents using elements delineated by tags, often paired with CSS and JavaScript — what is it?
HTML: Markup language for documents. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
This inflammation of the liver can cause jaundice and, if it becomes chronic, progress to cirrhosis — most commonly caused by five different viruses labeled A through E. What condition is it?
Hepatitis: Inflammation of the liver. Hepatitis is acute if it resolves within six months, and chronic if it lasts longer than six months.
The most widespread of all primates, this bipedal, nearly hairless species owes its advanced technology, culture, and language to a large, complex brain — what is it?
Human: Species of hominid in the genus Homo.

This crystalline mineral form of frozen water occurs naturally on Earth, other planets, and even in Oort cloud objects, and has at least nineteen known phases depending on temperature and pressure — what is it?
Ice: Frozen water; the solid state of water.

Native to the Americas but now grown worldwide, one species of this flowering plant genus has become such a popular ornamental that it's classified as an invasive weed on four continents — which genus?
Jacaranda: Genus of trees. The generic name is also used as the common name.
The youngest division chief in GM history shepherded the Pontiac GTO before founding the motor company behind a stainless-steel sports car immortalized in Back to the Future — who was he?
John DeLorean: American automobile engineer and executive (1925–2005)
Smaller, seedier, and more aromatic than its Persian cousin, this citrus hybrid lends its tart flavor to a beloved Florida pie named after the island chain it's associated with — what is it?
Key lime: Citrus fruit and plant.
Weighing up to 1,100 pounds, this heaviest of all non-crocodilian reptiles lacks a bony shell, its carapace covered instead in oily, leather-like flesh — what animal is it?
Leatherback sea turtle: Species of marine reptile.
Nicknamed for the Greek goddess of wisdom, this roughly 22-centimeter nocturnal bird was introduced to Britain in the late 1800s and to New Zealand's South Island soon after — which species?
Little owl: Species of owl. It was introduced into Britain at the end of the 19th century and into the South Island of New Zealand in the early 20th century.
Developed by MathWorks and named for its focus on matrix manipulations, this proprietary numeric computing environment powers the add-on Simulink for model-based design. What's it called?
MATLAB: Numerical computing environment and programming language.
Whether a milk board's 'Got Milk?' campaign or a city pitching itself as a tourist destination, this discipline boils down to acquiring, satisfying, and retaining customers — what is it?
Marketing: Study and process of exploring, creating, and delivering value to customers.
This WWII German monoplane fighter formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe alongside the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, though Allied aircrew nicknamed it after its designer — which aircraft?

Messerschmitt Bf 109: German WWII fighter aircraft family. The Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).
Nicknamed the 'sensitive plant,' this legume's leaves fold inward within seconds of being touched and reopen a few minutes later — what plant is it?
Mimosa pudica: Species of creeping annual plant.
This cancer attacks plasma cells — the white blood cells that normally make antibodies — often silently at first before bringing bone pain, anemia, and kidney trouble. What is it?
Multiple myeloma: Cancer of plasma cells. There is an increased risk of multiple myeloma in certain occupations, due to occupational exposure to aromatic hydrocarbon solvents.
Also called roundworms, these mostly free-living animals have a tubular digestive tract with openings at both ends and are grouped with arthropods in the clade Ecdysozoa — what are they?

A French apothecary and physician who studied at Avignon until the plague closed it, he's far better remembered for 942 cryptic quatrains said to foretell the future — by what Latinised name is he known?
Nostradamus: French apothecary, astrologer and seer (1503–1566)
Common in adolescents during growth spurts, this condition causes a painful bump just below the knee from inflammation where the patellar ligament attaches to the shinbone — what is it?

Osgood–Schlatter disease: Inflammation of the patellar ligament. Osgood–Schlatter disease (OSD) is inflammation of the patellar ligament at the tibial tuberosity (apophysitis) usually affecting adolescents during growth spurts.

Native across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this medium-sized game bird's family ties are murkier than expected — genetically, some species lean toward pheasants, others toward junglefowl. What bird is it?
Partridge: Common name for a type of bird.
Synthesized in 1938 by German chemist Otto Eisleb and later marketed as Demerol, this synthetic opioid was the go-to pain medication for much of the 20th century — what is it?
Pethidine: Opioid analgesic. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.

Often stereotyped as ferocious predators, these South American freshwater fish actually have varied diets that include plant matter, making them more omnivorous than their reputation suggests. What fish are they?
Piranha: Common name for certain fishes of the family Serrasalmidae.
Chickens, turkeys, ducks, and geese all fall under this term for birds domesticated for meat, eggs, or feathers — what is it called?
Poultry: Domesticated birds kept by humans for their eggs, meat or feathers.

Described as 'the translation of politics into the reality that citizens experience every day,' this field implements government policies and programs to solve social and economic problems — what is it called?
Public administration: Academic discipline; implementation or management of policy.
Native to the southern United States, this pond terrapin is the world's most commonly traded and most invasive turtle, largely due to pet releases — which species?
This American neuroscientist and primatologist, a Stanford professor across three departments, has spent his career studying the neuroendocrinology of stress — who is he?
Containing the potent compound salvinorin A, this plant used by Mazatec shamans for spiritual healing sparked a US media panic around 2007 after being shared in online videos — which plant?
Salvia divinorum: Species of plant. The leaves contain the potent compound salvinorin A and can induce a dissociative state and hallucinations.
Broader than linguistics, this field studies how signs — from words to maps to clothing — form systems that carry meaning, split into syntactics, semantics, and pragmatics — what is it called?
Semiotics: Study of signs. It is an interdisciplinary field that examines what signs are, how they form sign systems, and how individuals use them to communicate meaning.
These slow-moving South American mammals hang upside down in rainforest canopies, are kin to anteaters, and — despite the "two-toed" label — all have three toes on each rear limb; what are they?
Sloth: Group of tree dwelling mammals noted for slowness.
The sole living member of its genus, this slender, long-legged antelope of southwest Africa sports a white face, a dark eye-to-mouth stripe, and backward-curving horns on both sexes — what is it?
Springbok: Antelope of southwest and south Africa. The springbok or springbuck (Antidorcas marsupialis) is an antelope found mainly in south and southwest Africa.
Described as the most economically important oxide of its element, this compound with the formula SO3 is a key precursor to sulfuric acid and to acid rain — what is it?
Sulfur trioxide: Chemical compound. Sulfur trioxide exists in several forms: gaseous monomer, crystalline trimer, and solid polymer.

Named after the mathematician who introduced it in 1715, this infinite sum built from a function's derivatives at a single point becomes a special case named for Colin Maclaurin when centered at zero — what is it?
Taylor series: Mathematical approximation of a function.
Colored metallic blue on top and silvery below for camouflage, this genus of warm-blooded ocean fish includes the giant Atlantic bluefin and eight of the true tuna species — what genus is it?
Thunnus: Genus of fishes. Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
Named for its three heads — medial, lateral, and long — which upper-arm muscle straightens the elbow when it contracts?
Triceps: Muscle on the back of the upper arm. The triceps, or triceps brachii (Latin for "three-headed muscle of the arm"), is a large muscle on the back of the upper limb of many vertebrates.
Also known by the common names bilberry, blaeberry, and whortleberry, this holarctic shrub produces edible blue fruit — what is it?
Tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless, this polar molecule's strong hydrogen bonding makes it the solvent inside every known living organism — yet it offers no food energy at all. What is it?
Water: Chemical compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
Based on how long Earth takes to orbit the Sun, this unit of time comes in tropical and sidereal forms differing by about 20 minutes, with leap years keeping our calendar in sync — what unit?

Year: Unit of time based on Earth's orbit. In scientific use, the tropical year (approximately 365 solar days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45 seconds) and the sidereal year (about 20 minutes longer) are more exact.
The symbol for molybdenum is Mo. Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.
What is the chemical symbol for nickel?
The symbol for nickel is Ni. Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.

In what year was Cole Sprouse born?
Cole Sprouse: Cole Mitchell Sprouse (born August 4, 1992) is an American actor.
In what year was Taron Egerton born?
Taron Egerton (EJ-ər-tən; born 10 November 1989) is a Welsh actor.
In what year was Anna Nicole Smith born?
Anna Nicole Smith: Smith started her modeling career as a Playboy magazine centerfold in May 1992 and won the title of 1993 Playmate of the Year.
In what year was Dennis Quaid born?
Dennis Quaid: Dennis William Quaid (born April 9, 1954) is an American actor.
In what year was Lily Collins born?
Lily Collins: Lily Jane Collins (born 18 March 1989) is an English and American actress.
In what year was Kevin Spacey born?
Kevin Spacey Fowler (born July 26, 1959) is an American actor.
In what year was Peter Dinklage born?
Peter Dinklage: Peter Hayden Dinklage (born June 11, 1969) is an American actor.
In what year was Ray Stevenson born?
Ray Stevenson: George Raymond Stevenson (25 May 1964 – 21 May 2023) was a British actor, best known for his film and television work.
In what year was Lindsay Lohan born?
Lindsay Lohan: Lindsay Dee Lohan ( LOH-ən; born July 2, 1986) is an American actress, singer, and songwriter.
In what year was Ridley Scott born?
